newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas softens on moderate weather, futures.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas softens on moderate weather, futures.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices drifted lower Tuesday as temperatures moderated across most of the U.S. and Henry Hub futures opened lower, market sources said.
Physical prices at the Henry Hub, La, on average were down three cents from Monday to $2.20-2.22 per mmBtu, while Transco (Station 65) was quoted mostly in the mid-to-high $2.20s.
NYMEX's June Henry Hub gas futures slipped 3.4 cents early to a low of $2.181, but by the afternoon the contract had recovered to about $2.23.
Meanwhile, maintenance on Transco's Texas line will continue to cut about 400 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) out of a total capacity of about 600 mmcfd through Thursday.
However, temperatures throughout most of the U.S., including Texas, are expected to hover around normal to below normal through this week, Weather Services Corp said.

Also, Mobil Corp said maintenance at its Mary Ann gas plant in Coden, Ala., is expected to last until mid-June. Total capacity of the plant is 380-390 mmcfd, and about 120 mmcfd is due back within a week.
South Texas prices slipped one cent to $2.10-2.12, while west Texas prices in the Permian basin fell by two cents to the high-$1.90s.
At the southern California border, prices also lost two cents to $2.15-2.17 as temperatures in the Southwest were expected to remain near normal through this week.
In the East, cooler-than-normal weather pushed New York city-gate prices about five cents lower to the mid-$2.40s.

The 1,100 megawatt (MW) Peach Bottom 2 nuclear unit in Pennsylvania was still operating at a reduced rate of 72 percent early Tuesday for maintenance, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said. Also, the 610 MW Nine Mile Point 1 unit in New York was holding at 25 percent power early Tuesday.
In the Appalachian region, prices eased by two cents to about $2.40 on Columbia and the low-$2.40s on CNG.
In the Midcontinent, where temperatures are still mostly below normal, prices slipped two cents to about $2.
Chicago city-gate was quoted in the mid-$2.20s, while Detroit city-gate prices were in the low-to-mid $2.30s.
